text: Applying the coaction twice to the module factor equals applying the coalgebra comultiplication to the coefficient factor. The tensor associator merely matches parenthesizations; it does not exchange factors. This is precisely the right-comodule coassociativity axiom in [EGNO Definition 1.20.2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41), here exposed as an equality of linear maps over a commutative semiring. Checks pass: [coassoc_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L90), [lTensor_counit_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L98).
Checks the vectorwise version of coassociativity.
Checks the companion counit law.

Contracting the right tensor factor by φ commutes with coacting on the left factor. On m⊗c, both sides are φ(c)ρ(m), so linearity proves the equality for every tensor. This respects the factor order of the [right coaction](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41) and requires neither a chosen tensor decomposition nor finite-dimensionality. Checks pass: [tensorComponent_rTensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L115), [tensorComponent_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L79).
Checks the equality on an arbitrary tensor.
Checks contraction of a pure tensor is scalar multiplication.

The endomorphism selected by a functional φ sends m to the contraction of ρ(m): if ρ(m)=Σmᵢ⊗cᵢ, the result is Σφ(cᵢ)mᵢ. The sum describes a finite tensor presentation, not a chosen basis. This directly implements the coefficient-factor convention of [right comodules](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41) over the stated commutative semiring. Checks pass: [tensorComponent_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L79), [coactComponent_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Convolution.lean#L35).
Checks the pure-tensor contraction formula.
Checks contraction by the counit recovers the original vector.

The regular right comodule of C has coaction exactly its comultiplication Δ. The coalgebra’s own coassociativity and counit laws therefore supply the comodule axioms. This identifies the regular example of [EGNO Definitions 1.20.1–2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); no basis, finite generation, cocommutativity or separate action of an algebra on C is being introduced. Checks pass: [coassoc_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L90), [lTensor_counit_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L98).
Checks the inherited coassociativity equation.
Checks the inherited counit equation.

Evaluating a comodule morphism or its underlying linear map gives exactly the same function. The extra field is a proof that it intertwines coactions, not additional values on vectors. This is the morphism convention in [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), instantiated with the right tensor functor; the equality does not assert that the morphism is injective. Checks pass: [ofClass_eq_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L211), [map_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L235).
Checks the alternative linear-map coercion agrees.
Checks the retained coaction compatibility on vectors.

Two comodule morphisms with the same underlying linear map are equal, because their remaining fields only prove coaction compatibility. This matches [Wisbauer’s comodule morphisms](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), which are ordinary maps satisfying a commuting diagram. Injectivity here concerns forgetting the morphism structure, not injectivity of each morphism as a function between modules. Checks pass: [ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L223), [coe_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L207).
Checks equality follows from equal vector values.
Checks the underlying functions are unchanged.

Comodule morphisms are equal when they agree on every vector. The underlying linear maps are then equal, and their compatibility proofs carry no extra mathematical data. This is the equality criterion for the morphisms of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); it compares maps between the same fixed coactions, without identifying different comodule structures. Checks pass: [toLinearMap_injective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L216), [coe_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L207).
Checks equality after forgetting to linear maps.
Checks the evaluated functions coincide with those linear maps.

A comodule morphism satisfies (f⊗id_C)ρ_M=ρ_N f: applying f to the module coordinate of a coaction equals coacting after f. This is exactly the commuting diagram in [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) for the functor M↦M⊗C. The coefficient coalgebra remains fixed, and neither injectivity nor surjectivity of f is assumed. Checks pass: [map_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L235), [comp_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L270).
Checks the commuting diagram on individual vectors.
Checks the underlying composite used for morphism composition.

The identity comodule morphism sends every vector to itself. Its linear map is the identity and its compatibility with coactions is immediate, giving the identity arrow in [Wisbauer’s comodule category](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). This is an evaluation equation for the existing module and coaction, not a new identification of carriers. Checks pass: [id_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L266), [id_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L276).
Checks the underlying identity linear map.
Checks the left identity law for morphism composition.

The composite g.comp f evaluates at m as g(f(m)). Compatibility with coactions follows by applying the two commuting diagrams successively, as required in [Wisbauer’s comodule category](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The order is f first, then g; this multiplication of maps is ordinary composition, distinct from convolution of functionals on C. Checks pass: [comp_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L270), [comp_assoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L286).
Checks the corresponding linear-map composition.
Checks associativity of the composed morphisms.

Forgetting the identity comodule morphism gives the identity linear map. This is a defining equation: the constructor retains the same module and uses trivial coaction compatibility. It matches the identity in [Wisbauer’s comodule category](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), with no choice of basis or additional structure hidden in the forgetful operation. Checks pass: [id_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L244), [comp_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L281).
Checks the identity on vectors.
Checks the right identity law for composition.

A bundled comodule carries the same addition and zero as its stored underlying semimodule. This instance exposes that existing additive commutative monoid; it constructs neither a quotient nor new operations. It matches the underlying-object part of [Wisbauer’s comodule category](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). Over a semiring, additive inverses are not assumed. Checks pass: [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L73), [forget₂_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L307).
Checks bundling retains the original coaction.
Checks forgetting recovers the underlying semimodule.

The scalar action on a bundled comodule is the action already stored in its underlying semimodule. Exposing that module instance preserves the operations used to make the coaction linear. This is the underlying-module convention of [Wisbauer’s comodule category](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), extended here to commutative semirings without assuming additive inverses. Checks pass: [forget₂_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L307), [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L73).
Checks the precise underlying semimodule.
Checks the coaction is unchanged by bundling.

This constructor packages a module with its already supplied right coaction as an object of the comodule category. Its carrier, addition, scalar multiplication and coaction remain unchanged. This realizes the object described by [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), with the functor M↦M⊗C; it does not choose among possible coactions on the same module. Checks pass: [of_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L73), [forget₂_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L307).
Checks the packaged coaction is the supplied one.
Checks the underlying semimodule is retained.

Viewing an existing comodule morphism as a categorical arrow does not alter its value on any vector. Both representations use the same underlying linear map and the same coaction-compatibility proof. This implements the arrows of [Wisbauer’s comodule category](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); bundling introduces no transport of carriers or change of coordinates. Checks pass: [hom_ofHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L144), [ofHom_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L162).
Checks the unbundled-to-bundled round trip.
Checks bundling also preserves composition.

Two arrows between the same bundled comodules are equal if they agree on all vectors. These arrows are precisely the existing colinear linear maps, so their pointwise equality determines the entire morphism. This matches [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); it requires neither a basis nor finite generation of the source module. Checks pass: [ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L223), [ofHom_hom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cat.lean#L151).
Checks the underlying comodule-morphism equality criterion.
Checks categorical and unbundled arrows have the same data.

Contracting a right coaction by the counit gives the identity endomorphism: applying ε to the coefficient factor recovers m. The tensor unitor turns m⊗1 into m. This is [EGNO’s counit axiom](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41) expressed through coaction components, valid here over a commutative semiring without any finite-dimensionality assumption. Checks pass: [lTensor_counit_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L98), [coactComponent_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L129).
Checks the counit equation before applying the tensor unitor.
Checks contraction is the actual component operation.

Contracting ρ by a functional defines an algebra homomorphism from the convolution dual to endomorphisms of M. Coassociativity gives T_(f*g)=T_f∘T_g and the counit gives identity. Here (f*g)(c)=Σf(c₁)g(c₂), the alternative convention explicitly noted in [Wisbauer §4.8](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=15); multiplication in the target is composition, not convolution. Checks pass: [coactComponent_coactComponent](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L134), [coactComponent_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Convolution.lean#L35).
Checks the contraction order yielding multiplicativity.
Checks preservation of the convolution unit.

The action of a convolution functional f on m is obtained by contracting the coefficient factor of ρ(m), giving Σf(cᵢ)mᵢ for any tensor presentation. The WithConv wrapper changes the multiplication on functionals, not their evaluation. This is the contraction mechanism of [Wisbauer §4.9](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=16), here using right coactions and f(c₁)g(c₂) convolution. Checks pass: [coactComponent_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L129), [tensorComponent_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L79).
Checks the contraction defining the action.
Checks evaluation on pure tensors.

A comodule morphism commutes with every convolution-dual operator: f(T_g m)=T_g(f(m)). Its coaction-compatibility equation remains valid after contracting the common coefficient factor. This is the morphism compatibility behind [Wisbauer §4.9](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=16), with right coactions here. Neither a faithful dual action nor injectivity or surjectivity of f is required. Checks pass: [map_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Basic.lean#L235), [tensorComponent_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L85).
Checks the uncontracted compatibility equation.
Checks contraction is natural under linear maps.

The zero comodule morphism has the zero linear map underneath. It is colinear because both coactions are linear and send zero to zero. This gives the zero arrow among the compatible linear maps of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); it does not require additive inverses or a zero source or target module. Checks pass: [zero_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L81), [zero_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L186).
Checks zero on every vector.
Checks composition with the zero morphism remains zero.

A specified map ρ on N inherits the [right-comodule axioms](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41) from an ambient comodule when an inclusion i intertwines coactions. The constructor requires both i and i⊗id_(C⊗C) injective: cancel the latter for coassociativity and i for the counit. No flatness is assumed; mere injectivity of i would not justify tensor cancellation. Checks pass: [ofInjective_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/OfInjective.lean#L77), [transport_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L81).
Checks the constructed coaction is exactly the supplied map.
Checks the linear-equivalence application, where tensor injectivity comes from an inverse.

The comodule inherited through an equivariant inclusion uses exactly the specified linear map ρ as its coaction. The constructor proves the [right-comodule identities](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41) rather than replacing that map. Its hypotheses still require injectivity of both i and i⊗id_(C⊗C); this equation does not weaken those cancellation conditions. Checks pass: [transport_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L81), [transportCoact_refl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L61).
Checks the inherited-map equation in the transport application.
Checks identity transport leaves the original coaction unchanged.

Transporting a coaction through e:M≃N sends n to (e⊗id_C)ρ(e⁻¹n). The formula changes the module coordinate while keeping the coefficient coalgebra fixed, respecting the [right-coaction convention](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). The inverse is supplied by the linear equivalence, so this operation needs no choice of basis or flatness of C. Checks pass: [transportCoact_refl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L61), [transportCoact_trans](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L100).
Checks identity transport.
Checks successive transports agree with the composite equivalence.

The comodule installed on N by transport along e has the conjugated coaction (e⊗id_C)ρe⁻¹. Tensoring e⁻¹ remains invertible, so the inherited-axioms constructor applies without flatness. This preserves the [right-comodule identities](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); the local instance specifies this transported structure, rather than asserting equality with an arbitrary coaction already on N. Checks pass: [transport_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Transport.lean#L89), [ofInjective_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/OfInjective.lean#L77).
Checks the installed coaction pointwise.
Checks the inheritance constructor retains its supplied linear map.

An extended nonnegative real raised to a natural-number exponent, viewed as a real exponent, equals its ordinary repeated product. This includes zero and infinity. Exponent zero gives 1 at either endpoint; a positive natural exponent preserves zero or infinity. The cast of the exponent is exact and performs no rounding or integer division. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L683).

Negating a real exponent takes the reciprocal of the extended nonnegative power. This holds for every base, including zero and infinity, because the extended reciprocal swaps those two endpoints. For example, 0^(−1)=∞ and ∞^(−1)=0. Exponent zero gives 1 on both sides, so no nonzero condition on the exponent is needed. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L649).

Raising an extended nonnegative real to real exponent −1 gives its extended reciprocal. Positive finite values have the ordinary reciprocal, while zero gives infinity and infinity gives zero. Thus the statement includes both endpoints without a nonzero hypothesis. Its zero-base value differs from ordinary real arithmetic, where the reciprocal of zero is assigned zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L664).

Taking an extended reciprocal and taking a real power commute. Every extended nonnegative base and every real exponent are allowed, including both endpoints and exponent zero. At zero or infinity, reciprocation swaps the endpoints, and the power’s sign rules agree with that swap. This does not assert that a base times its reciprocal always equals 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L757).

For every extended nonnegative base, multiplying two real exponents agrees with taking the two powers successively. Both exponents may be zero or negative, and zero and infinity are valid bases. Their sign-dependent power values make the identity hold even when an intermediate power is infinity; no conversion to an ordinary real is involved. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L666).

Adding two arbitrary real exponents multiplies their powers when the extended base is positive and finite. Both endpoint exclusions matter. With base zero or infinity and exponents 1 and −1, the left side is 1, whereas the right side is 0·∞=0. The hypotheses keep the law on its usual positive finite domain. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L623).

For nonnegative real exponents, their sum gives the product of the corresponding powers for every extended nonnegative base, including zero and infinity. Zero exponents are allowed and contribute the factor 1. Requiring both exponents to be nonnegative prevents the opposing-sign endpoint cases that can otherwise turn the product into 0·∞=0. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L630).

For a positive finite extended base, subtracting real exponents gives the quotient of the corresponding powers. The subtraction is ordinary real subtraction, not truncated subtraction of extended nonnegative values. Excluding zero and infinity avoids endpoint failures: with equal exponents 1, the left side is 1 but either 0/0 or ∞/∞ is assigned zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L661).

A nonnegative real power distributes over multiplication of any two extended nonnegative values, including zero and infinity. At exponent zero both sides equal 1. The exponent restriction excludes a real failure: for exponent −1 and factors zero and infinity, the left side is infinity while the product of the powers is ∞·0=0. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L737).

For two finite extended nonnegative factors, any real power distributes over their product. Zero factors and negative exponents are allowed; the resulting powers may be infinite. Finiteness here concerns the original factors only. It rules out the zero-times-infinity input combination responsible for failure of unrestricted multiplicativity at negative exponents. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L720).

A nonnegative real power distributes over an extended quotient, even when the denominator is zero or infinity. Division multiplies by the extended reciprocal: 0/0 and ∞/∞ are zero. These defaults agree on both sides; exponent zero gives 1. Negative exponents are excluded, since for 0/0 with exponent −1 the two sides would differ. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L766).

For any nonzero real y, first raising an extended nonnegative value to exponent 1/y and then to exponent y returns the original value. Negative y is allowed, and zero or infinity as the base is allowed. The reciprocal exponent is an ordinary real reciprocal; its nonzero hypothesis prevents both powers from collapsing to exponent zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L982).

Raising an extended nonnegative value to a nonzero real exponent y and then to exponent 1/y recovers the value. This includes negative exponents and both endpoints. For example, reciprocal powers swap zero and infinity twice. The nonzero condition is essential in general: with y=0 both successive powers give 1 regardless of the starting value. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L979).

For a positive real y, the map x↦x^y is an increasing bijection of the extended nonnegative reals, with inverse x↦x^(1/y). Zero and infinity are fixed. Thus it preserves and reflects order as well as recovering every input through the inverse. Positivity excludes exponent zero, which is constant, and negative exponents, which reverse order. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L784).

For a fixed positive real exponent, comparing the powers of two extended nonnegative values is equivalent to comparing the original values. Zero and infinity are included, and the implication works in both directions. Strict positivity matters: exponent zero sends every base to 1, while a negative exponent reverses order rather than preserving it. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L801).

For positive real z, the inequality x^(1/z)≤y is equivalent to x≤y^z throughout the extended nonnegative reals. Zero and infinity require no extra exclusions because positive powers fix them. Here 1/z is ordinary real division by a positive number; it is not integer division, and the inequality direction is preserved. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L815).

For positive real z, the inequality x≤y^(1/z) is equivalent to x^z≤y, allowing zero and infinity on either side. This is the usual operation of taking a positive root or raising both sides to a positive power. The reciprocal exponent uses real arithmetic; positivity ensures that applying the power does not reverse the inequality. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L812).

For an extended nonnegative base at least 1, increasing a real exponent cannot decrease the power. Infinity is permitted: its powers are zero, 1, or infinity according as the exponent is negative, zero, or positive. This is a weak inequality; the base 1 is constant, and infinity also has constant ranges of exponents. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L846).

For an extended nonnegative base at most 1, increasing a real exponent cannot increase the power. Zero is included: its powers descend from infinity for negative exponents, to 1 at zero, to zero for positive exponents. No positive-base hypothesis is needed for this weak inequality; at base 1 all powers are equal. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L863).

For a nonnegative real base and nonnegative real exponent, including the base into extended nonnegative reals commutes with taking its power. Zero bases and zero exponents are allowed. The exponent guard avoids a mismatch at zero: a negative power of zero is zero in ordinary reals but infinity in the extended type. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L968).

Every nonzero affinoid algebra A over a complete nonarchimedean field contains an injective image of some Tate algebra K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ and is finitely generated as a module through that map. Affinoid means an algebraic quotient of a finite-variable Tate algebra; no quotient norm is chosen. Nilpotents are allowed. The zero algebra is explicitly excluded. See [Bosch, §2.2 Corollary11, p.19](https://math.bu.edu/people/yangzhe/Bosch_FormalRigidGeometry.pdf#page=26). Checks pass through [the explicit polynomial quotient comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Weierstrass/Quotient.lean#L126) and [finite free quotients](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Weierstrass/Quotient.lean#L193) for Y²−X³, plus [constant norms](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/TateAlgebra/Basic.lean#L266) and the zero quotient for non-injectivity. These are specializations of existing formulas.
The quotient comparison preserves polynomial representatives and the coefficient map
The distinguished quadratic quotient is finite over its coefficient Tate algebra
The distinguished quotient retains a free module structure
Monomial norms compute the cusp coefficient bound
Constants distinguish zero and one in every Tate algebra

For every affinoid algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field, each prime ideal equals the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it. Equivalently, every radical ideal has that property. This is an algebraic statement independent of a chosen norm on the quotient. Nilpotents are retained, and the zero algebra is allowed: an empty intersection of ideals is the whole ring. See [Bosch, §3.1 Proposition3(ii), p.32](https://math.bu.edu/people/yangzhe/Bosch_FormalRigidGeometry.pdf#page=38). Checks pass via [quotient constructions](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Affinoid/Basic.lean#L65), [monic quotient comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Weierstrass/Quotient.lean#L126) for X², and [the native nonzero nilpotent example](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Examples/RingTheory/Affinoid/MinimalPolynomial.lean#L57). The audit spells out the zero-ring and dual-number ideal computations.
Quotients include the zero and unit ideals without a nontriviality assumption
The native dual-number example retains the nonzero nilpotent and its quadratic minimal equation
